title: Frequency
summary:
Training frequency is the number of exercise sessions in a given period, usually days per week. The recommended frequency depends on prior fitness and stage of pregnancy. International consensus says healthy pregnant women should do at least 150 min of moderate-intensity activity per week, spread over three or more days, ideally every day.

Clinical guidelines advise moderate activity 3-5 days a week, which gives significant benefit without compromising maternal or fetal health, and greater adherence leads to better outcomes. The chapter gives frequencies by trimester and by profile (sedentary, active, athlete), and stresses listening to the body and allowing recovery.
points: Healthy pregnant women should perform at least 150 min of moderate-intensity activity per week, over three or more days, ideally every day.
Guidelines advise moderate activity 3-5 days a week.
Greater adherence to and frequency of training lead to better maternal-fetal outcomes.
In the first trimester, without complications, women can keep their prepregnancy frequency and adjust intensity to how they feel.
In the second and third trimesters, keep 3-5 days per week, prioritizing low-impact exercise and avoiding fall or abdominal trauma risks.
Sedentary women can start with low-intensity sessions two to three times per week.
Active women can continue three to four times per week if there are no contraindications.
Pregnant athletes can train 5-7 days a week, with constant medical supervision and adjustments as pregnancy progresses.
takeaways: Use 150 min per week of moderate activity across 3 or more days as the baseline.
Sedentary women should begin gradually, 2-3 sessions per week.
Choose low-impact activities in the second and third trimesters.
Plan recovery between sessions to avoid excessive fatigue.
Adjust frequency to individual needs, trimester and prior fitness level.
Combine regular activity with sufficient rest.
cautions: Stop exercising immediately if dizziness, bleeding, chest pain or difficulty breathing appear.
Avoid overexertion and activities with risk of falls or abdominal trauma.
